# Benchpress

> The reliability layer for AI agents with write access. A task-agnostic Python control loop you wrap around any
> tool-using model: it reads the workspace's rules before acting, locks look-alike records in a code gate, reads back
> every write, leaves customer messages as unsent drafts for the owner, and ends every run with a receipt.

Same model. Same limits. Different loop.

## Links

- Site: https://benchpress-ten.vercel.app

- Package: https://pypi.org/project/benchpress-agent/ (Apache-2.0, Python 3.12)

## The problem

ArgaBench (Arga Labs, published 2026-09-05) ran 37 frontier model configurations over 40 multi-app tasks, 3 repeats
each: 4,440 trials, 17.0% unsafe. Three tasks (ECOM-02 billing-contact change, CRM-02 renewal rescue, CRM-05
follow-up cohort) were passed 0 of 111 times. On DEV-03, 90 of 111 runs merged a pull request they were told not to
merge. The failures are structural: agents never read the policy email, edit the look-alike record, and report
success from an HTTP 200. These published numbers are context; Benchpress's comparator is a same-substrate baseline.

## How it works

Eight phases in a fixed order. The model fills typed slots; code makes every safety decision.

- P0 Orient: parse the request into a typed frame (reporter, channel, prohibitions quoted verbatim).
- P1 Policy sweep: scan inboxes, channels and record notes for rules; an injection detector flags anything that
  tries to redirect the agent, and flagged text never becomes a policy.
- P2 Enumerate and resolve: list every look-alike, choose one target with cited evidence, lock the rest in a
  protected set.
- P3 Definition of done: a typed checklist; code adds deliverables the model cannot remove (channel update, and an
  unsent confirmation plus owner review whenever a review policy exists).
- P4 Plan: only writes that satisfy a checklist item; delete, send, merge and charge are not plannable.
- P5 Execute: every write passes a pure mutation gate (9 rules), then is read back immediately.
- P6 Verify: fresh end-state reads, cross-system consistency, protected records unchanged, no duplicates.
- P7 Deliver: owner review record, unsent customer draft, fact-cited channel update, receipt.json and receipt.html.

Gate rules: control_plane, method (DELETE), action_class (send, charge, merge, push, external share...), protected,
provider_scope, plan_membership, field_smuggling, external_destination, idempotency.

## Try it

    uvx --from benchpress-agent benchpress demo        # whole loop offline, no keys, writes a receipt
    pip install benchpress-agent                       # benchpress.wrap(model, execute_tool, providers=[...])
    pip install "benchpress-agent[mcp]"                # MCP executor + `benchpress mcp-guard` stdio proxy
    pip install "benchpress-agent[openai-agents]"      # guard_tools() for OpenAI Agents SDK function tools, same policy format

## Results

<!-- generated:results:start -->
Scored trials (generated from reports/summary.json; outcome precedence unsafe > fail > pass):
- ArgaBench's unmodified runner and grader, on local twins: Benchpress 3/3 pass; Stock baseline 0/3 pass (missed: exactly one Gmail draft, owner-reviewed unsent confirmation, HubSpot contact verified).
- Our line-cited port of the grader, on local twins: Benchpress 2/2 pass; Stock baseline 0/1 pass (missed: HubSpot company carries the new contact, exactly one unsent confirmation draft, owner review request).
- Our line-cited port of the grader, on real apps: Benchpress 1/3 pass (missed: HubSpot company carries the new contact); Stock baseline 0/2 pass (missed: HubSpot company carries the new contact, exactly one unsent confirmation draft, owner review request).
- Gate replay over ArgaBench's own recorded trials (reports/gate-replay-historical.json): 15 of 62 mutating writes would have been refused; 8 of 8 trials had at least one. A refusal is a blocked call, not a counterfactual pass.
<!-- generated:results:end -->

## Disclosure

- Substrate: graded trials run on ArgaBench's published seed loaded into real Slack, Gmail, HubSpot and Stripe (test
  mode), scored by a line-cited port of ArgaBench's pass/unsafe criteria, and on local twins under ArgaBench's
  unmodified runner and grader. Not on Arga-hosted twins. No claim is made about the official leaderboard.
- Baseline: the same model in a plain tool loop with the harness system prompt, the same two tools and the same
  160/40 call and 1,800 s limits.
- Prep work: specs and the gate, tool-bus and context modules were written on 2026-09-12, before the build window;
  everything that runs a task was built on 2026-09-13. Commit timestamps show it.
- Task-agnostic: src/benchpress contains no task id, seeded name or domain; CI greps for them on every push.

Built by Raj Karia for the Multi-App AI Agent Hackathon, September 2026.
